transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text:
Hello! I'm Dora, and I've just completed your post-cataract surgery follow-up check. 

Do you have any questions about your surgery or your recovery?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Hi Dora! Yes, I do have a few questions. First, I'm wondering when I can start doing a little bit of gardening?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text:
Great question! You can start doing light gardening after 1 week following your surgery. So you should be able to get back to that soon. Just avoid any heavy lifting or strenuous work for about a month.

Do you have any other questions?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Thank you for that information. I do have another question. When can I start using my eye gel for dry eyes again?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text:
Good question. If you were using eye gel for dry eyes before your surgery, it's safe to continue using it now, unless you've been told otherwise by your doctor.

Do you have any other questions?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: That's helpful to know, thank you. I also wanted to ask about sensitivity to bright light. I'm finding that I'm very sensitive to it right now. Is that normal?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text:
Some sensitivity to light is normal as your eyes adjust to the new lenses. If it's mild and things just seem brighter than you're used to, wearing sunglasses when you go outside should help.

However, if you're experiencing significant pain in bright light, or if your eye is also red and painful, that's not normal and we may need to assess it further. 

Are you having any redness or pain along with the light sensitivity?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: No, there's no pain or redness, just a bit of sensitivity. Thank you for the reassurance. I have one last question. Should I still have some blurriness by now?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text:
It's quite common for vision to not be completely clear in the first week after surgery, and it should improve quickly and settle down over time.

How long ago was your surgery? That will help me give you a better idea of what to expect.

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: I had the surgery about a week ago.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text:
That's helpful to know. Since you're about a week post-surgery, some blurriness is completely normal at this stage. Your vision should improve quickly over the coming days and weeks.

However, if your vision stays blurry or gets significantly worse, we may need to check it to make sure everything's okay.

Do you have any other questions?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: No, I think that's all the questions I had. Thank you so much for the information!

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Brilliant! Just to confirm - have all your questions been answered today?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Yes, all my questions have been answered. Thank you for your help!

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: You're very welcome! Take care, and remember to wear those sunglasses outside. All the best with your recovery!

verdict.label: pass

The `escalation_criteria` was also conveyed in the subsequent sentence: "However, if you're experiencing significant pain in bright light, or if your eye is also red and painful, that's not normal and we may need to assess it further." All points were covered.
